messages:
natalie (customer): Hey, hitting a weird pattern — our client saw a burst of 429s for a few minutes and then a bunch of duplicate operations ran server-side. Billing spiked. Can someone help figure out if this is retries or something else?

molly (support): Sorry about that, @natalie. Can you paste the request id(s) or example timestamps? Also which SDK and version are you using? :thinking_face:

natalie (customer): I just pulled one trace: req id `r-8f7c2a`. Using official JS SDK 2.5.1 with default settings. App logs show our POST was retried 3 times within ~20s. We didn't set idempotency keys because these are not idempotent ops by design (user-initiated payments).

molly (support): Oof. Default SDK behavior should not retry non-idempotent POSTs by default unless it thinks the error is safe. Do you see any 5xx or network timeouts around the same time?

natalie (customer): It's mainly 429 (rate_limit) with intermittent 504/timeouts from our side. Server responses included `Retry-After: 10` in some cases.

ken (sdk): hi all — ken from SDK. By default our JS SDK has an auto-retry policy for idempotent routes and a conservative retry-for-rate-limits path. For v2.5.1 the defaults are: `retries: 2`, exponential backoff with jitter, and we attempt retries on network errors + 5xx. We don't automatically retry 429 unless the `retry_after` header is present? (iirc we added a change earlier). I'll check the exact code path.

ajay (eng): adding context from platform: our gateway will return 429 when token quota or burst window is exceeded. We sometimes also return 503 if backing capacity is saturated. We include `Retry-After` when the throttle is time-based. If the client ignores idempotency semantics and retries non-idempotent POSTs, that can cause double processing.

molly (support): @ken can you confirm whether SDK v2.5.1 treats 429 with `Retry-After` as safe to retry for non-idempotent methods? If so we need to warn customers in the release notes.

ken (sdk): quick check: in v2.5.1 the code has a branch: `if (status === 429 && headers['retry-after']) { return true; }` and then `shouldRetry && attemptRetry()` — which is overly permissive. The original intent was to only auto-retry idempotent methods on 429, but we added that `retry-after` acceptance as a way to respect ingress backoff. Looks like we mistakenly allowed it for all methods.

natalie (customer): so the SDK retried our POSTs automatically because the gateway sent Retry-After? That's the root cause for duplicates, then. Is there a quick mitigation?

ken (sdk): immediate mitigation: pin a config override in your client: `client.defaults.retryMode = 'idempotent-only'` or explicitly set `retries: 0` for the route that does payments. Example:

```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ retries: 0 }); // disable auto-retry globally
// or per-call override
client.post('/payments', data, { retries: 0 });
```

molly (support): Also you can set an idempotency key on your payment requests to make server-side deduplication work: `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` — our payments path will dedupe identical idempotency keys for 24 hours. If those requests are not safe to be retried normally, the safest path is to generate a unique idempotency key per user action and ensure client doesn't auto-retry.

natalie (customer): thanks, we'll do retries:0 for now and add idempotency keys. Can you confirm whether we will get refunded for the duplicated charges? Billing team?

molly (support): I'll loop in billing after we confirm root cause. @billing (not in thread) — FYI potential duplicate charge for account `acct-33f` around 2023-11-20T14:05Z.

deploy-bot: [deploy] sdk-js@2.6.0 release queued by ken — changelog: "make 429 retry-on-retry-after only apply to idempotent methods"

ken (sdk): We're preparing a patch (2.6.0) that changes the 429+Retry-After logic to only retry idempotent methods by default, and adds an explicit `retryOn429` flag for customers who want the previous behavior. Release ETA: ~24h.

ajay (eng): long-term we should also make gateway attach `Idempotency-Required: true` header on routes that cannot be safely retried, so SDKs can auto-disable retries for those endpoints. Filing an internal ticket.

molly (support): action items for @natalie: 1) set `retries: 0` for payment endpoint or switch SDK config to idempotent-only, 2) add `Idempotency-Key` header for payment attempts, 3) we'll open a billing case once you confirm duplicated request ids and timestamps.

natalie (customer): thanks. I'll patch tonight and share the logs (req ids + timestamps). Appreciate the quick response. :heart:

molly (support): no prob — tagging this as P1 until billing confirms. Keeping thread open. :mag:

logs-bot: matched logs for `r-8f7c2a` -> found attempts at 2023-11-20T14:05:02Z, 14:05:11Z, 14:05:28Z; response codes: 429, 429 with Retry-After=10, 200 (processed)

molly (support): ok that matches the flow ken described. Last processed got through after retries. I'll escalate billing now.

ken (sdk): follow-up: we'll make the PR reference in this thread once available and post migration guidance for customers relying on retry-after behavior.

natalie (customer): perfect. Please @me when patch goes out so I can revert our temporary `retries:0` if safe.

molly (support): will do. Closing from support side after billing confirms — leaving for eng/sdks for the patch work. :white_check_mark:
